correctness.rationale: For each real row the Rademacher average is minimized at equal absolute coordinates by Jensen, strictly unless flat in even dimension (balanced sign witness). Saturation forces flat rows and constancy of convolution with the absolute-sign-sum function. For every nontrivial even Walsh character, the cosine integral representation has an integrable sign-definite coefficient and is nonzero. Finite-group Fourier inversion therefore forces equal positive weights in all 2^(n−1) antipodal classes. Conversely uniform weights attain the bound, and compactness yields strictness below the threshold. The checker reproduces finite examples exactly but the proof is dimension-uniform.
